scope_note: This is not a species-complete catalogue of every extremophile on Earth. It covers the major extremophile classes with representative organisms selected for mechanistic evidence and cross-domain diversity.
frozen_question: Which functional survival modules recur across the major extremophile classes, and which are specific to organisms that survive extremes by reversible dormancy rather than active homeostasis?

major_classes.dominant_stress: high external pH, often plus salt

representative_models.high_value_observation: Extreme radiation survival is not explained by preventing DNA breaks alone; proteome protection and efficient genome repair/reassembly are central.

Rapid-desiccation-tolerant tardigrade uses constitutive heat-soluble protective proteins and reversible tun-state architecture; movement can resume within minutes after rehydration in laboratory protocols.
sources: Nature Communications 2026 CAHS12 synthetic-cell protection study

representative_models.high_value_observation: After severe ionizing radiation, measurable DNA damage falls substantially during a 24-h recovery period, showing strong post-damage repair rather than complete damage avoidance.
Desiccation can produce major DSB accumulation; repair is activated on rehydration, with strong early transcriptional repair response and genomic recovery over hours to days.
Anhydrobiotic larvae vitrify/stabilize cellular contents; rehydration itself causes a strong oxidative pulse, yet damage is repaired within hours and activity rapidly resumes.
Dormant spores cannot actively repair accumulated lesions; repair factors are packaged or induced during germination/outgrowth and lesions must be processed as metabolism and replication restart.
Dehydration and rehydration are distinct molecular states; much of the transcriptional program returns near hydrated baseline by ~24 h and photosynthetic physiology recovers over ~48 h.
Desert strains combine pigments/ROS protection, protein protection, DNA repair, biofilm shielding and ametabolic dry states; post-rehydration repair remains an active 2026 research target.
Dehydrated black fungus survives combinations of cold, radiation, vacuum and Mars-like conditions; melanization/envelope robustness and low-metabolic states are major protective layers.
Maintains function under extreme salinity using archaeal osmoadaptation, stress regulation and robust DNA-repair systems; no obligatory dormant exit is required.
Lives near pH 0 using exceptionally proton-tight membranes, acid-stable envelope/proteins and high energetic investment in internal pH maintenance.
Combines osmotic balance with Na+/H+ and ion-cycling strategies to remain metabolically active in high salt and alkaline pH.
Remains metabolically active in subzero conditions using flexible membranes, osmolytes, protein-folding changes and increased DNA-repair investment.
Obligate piezophilic hyperthermophile adapts through whole-system metabolic and membrane tuning rather than a single repair switch.
Uses compatible-solute retention, membrane/cell-wall remodeling and integrated stress signaling to sustain growth at very low water activity.
Extreme metal tolerance is dominated by rapid efflux, complexation/reduction and distributed resistance loci rather than dormancy.

cross_class_modules.comment: Every major class requires some combination of shielding, redox control, compartment chemistry or structural stabilization to keep damage below catastrophic levels.

Chaperones, intrinsically disordered protectants, compatible solutes, pigments/antioxidants or chemically adapted proteins recur broadly. Deinococcus is a key negative control against DNA-only thinking.
Especially dominant in active thermophiles, psychrophiles, halophiles, acidophiles, alkaliphiles, piezophiles and osmophiles.
Widespread across classes, but survival may depend more strongly on preserving repair proteins and cellular chemistry than on avoiding DNA lesions.
Strong in anhydrobiotes, spores, resurrection plants and some desert microbes; absent as a requirement in many continuously active extremophiles.
Trehalose/LEA glasses, tardigrade CAHS assemblies, spore dehydration/rigidity and related mechanisms stabilize structures when normal aqueous biochemistry cannot operate.

Damage repair and biochemical normalization are concentrated after rehydration/germination in multiple independent lineages. This is an abstract recovery gate, not evidence for a shared molecular switch.
